question: For the purpose of enhancing the Strategy for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities up to 2030, the Commission conducted an online public consultation between November 2025 and February 2026. The call was made available in all EU official languages and in an easy-toread format; however, it was not accessible in sign language on the Commission’s homepage.

This is despite the fact that, in its 2025 Concluding Observations, the Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) recommended that the EU apply the same accessibility standards it requires of Member States and implement comprehensive accessibility measures across all platforms, including sign language interpretation, irrespective of the topic. 1.

Was any technical facility provided to enable deaf persons using sign language to submit feedback, and is the Commission planning any solution, based on human translation or AI, that would facilitate the processing of feedback provided in sign language?
How does the Commission justify the absence of sign language accessibility for the 2025–2026 public consultation on the disability rights strategy, given its stated commitment to the CRPD standards?

What concrete timeline has the Commission established to ensure that the EU’s main home page fully complies with accessibility standards for persons with disabilities, including those who rely on sign language?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.5.2026) The Commission, through the Strategy for the rights of persons with disabilities 2021-2030 is advancing to address the needs of persons with disabilities, including deaf persons. This Strategy will be further enhanced by an upcoming Communication. The Commission is committed to lead by example as a public administration.

In 2024 and 2025, it provided International Sign at 60 press conferences and midday briefings and at 14 events1. The consultation process for the enhanced Strategy included different meetings with stakeholders, in which International Sign was available for providing feedback. However, as the open public consultation was done in writing format; hence it only sought written feedback.

In this regard, it accommodated different accessibility needs by providing a standard and easy-to-read (ETR) form2 to fill online, and offline with an accessible word document to send by email. ETR versions for the call for evidence and the Have Your Say data protection statement were also provided.

Since 2022, the Commission has been updating and aligning its web presence to comply with the European accessibility standard EN 301 549, which does not require the provision of sign language as an alternative or complement to content in text or video. The Commission is nevertheless working on increasing the availability of International Sign in video.
For example, the weekly College readout and the live broadcast of the President’s State of the Union include International Sign.
1 Including, for example, the Erasmus+ Sport Info Day or the European Day of Persons with Disabilities
Conference. 2 The standard forms and the easy-to-read versions were provided in all EU languages.
